Note::is_float64¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::is_float64() const noexcept

Recognize Native Floating-Point Notes¶

is_float64() reports whether the receiver stores IEEE 754 double-precision lanes. It is a dtype query, not a value classifier: an Int64 Note is not Float64 even when every integer is exactly representable as a double, and a Text Note containing "0.25" is still Text.

Natural-language scores and other continuous Note results use Float64 storage. After the check succeeds, reals() exposes a borrowed contiguous std::span<const double> without conversion or allocation. Rank, empty shape, finite values, infinities, and NaNs do not change the answer. Undefined returns false; the method is constant-time and noexcept.

Example 1: Float64 Is Distinct From Int64¶

const auto scores = pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{0.25, 0.75});
const auto integers = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{0, 1});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scores=" << scores.is_float64()
          << " integers=" << integers.is_float64() << '\n';

Output¶

scores=true integers=false

Example 2: Absence Is Not A Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "absent=" << pluss::Note::undefined().is_float64() << '\n';

Output¶

absent=false

Example 3: The Check Does Not Read Values¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<double>{0.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
                        std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN()});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << values.is_float64()
          << " lanes=" << values.numel() << '\n';

Output¶

true lanes=3

See Also¶

  • Note::dtype: obtain NoteDType::Float64 directly.

  • Note::reals(): borrow the native double lanes after checking the dtype.

  • Note::is_int64: the integral numeric dtype.
